name: UptimeRobot
summary: Uptime monitoring with a generous free tier: website, port, keyword and API checks down to 60-second intervals, status pages, integrations and mobile apps.
best_for: solo builders and small teams monitoring sites, ports and APIs at 60-second resolution with status pages, and honestly, the free 50-monitor tier covers most hobby stacks
skip_if: you need many teammates in the dashboard (seats are a paid add-on) or heavy SMS alerting: credits stack on top of the subscription
honest_knock: The famous free tier is real, but the paid ladder has quiet extras: extra login seats cost $15-19 per month EACH beyond the included ones, and SMS or voice-call alerts are pay-per-credit on every plan. The Solo tier includes no team seats at all.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-08-26 on uptimerobot.com/pricing over a US connection; re-read 2026-09-29 and 2026-11-28 from a European connection, where the page and its machine-readable pricing.md serve euro amounts identical to our 17 August euro reading, so the dollar figures here could not be re-read from Europe) Free is $0. Solo starts at $144 a year, Team is $468 and Scale starts at $948 — the page quotes yearly, not monthly, which makes it look cheaper per line than it is against monthly-priced rivals. Login seats are the upsell: none on Solo, three on Team, five on Scale, and more at $15 or $19 each a month. Data retention runs three months on Free, twelve on Solo and twenty-four above that. They publish a machine-readable version of this page for AI agents, which is rare enough to be worth noting. New since August: paid plans add monitoring of the third-party services you depend on — 1-5 on Solo, 20 on Team and 40-100 on Scale by monitor tier — which the pricing page listed as launching in September 2026; on 28 November 2026 pricing.md lists it as included on every paid plan, with the same counts.

sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 15 November 2026 the session tested UptimeRobot on the free plan: how fast a free monitor alerts on a failing page, the limits of the free plan, the price of the cheapest paid plan up to the card form, and the way to delete the account. Nothing was paid and nothing was deleted. A new HTTP monitor was created for a page on our own site that returns 404 (checked). It was created at 17:16:38. At 17:17:36 the dashboard still said Preparing and showed 100% for the last 24 hours with 0 incidents. The DOWN email, Monitor is DOWN for that page, arrived at 17:17:45, about 67 seconds after the monitor was created, although the free interval is 5 minutes. At 17:23:30 the dashboard said Down, currently down for 0h 5m 56s, with 1 incident and 16.6% uptime over 24 hours. The test monitor was paused afterwards and not deleted. The monitor for our own site, created in the onboarding, keeps running. No kit records were entered.
findings: A free HTTP monitor on a page of our own site that returns 404 was created at 17:16:38. The DOWN email, Monitor is DOWN, arrived at 17:17:45, about 67 seconds later, although the free check interval is 5 minutes. At 17:17:36 the dashboard still said Preparing with 100% and 0 incidents.
At 17:23:30 the dashboard said Down, currently down for 5 minutes and 56 seconds, with 1 incident and 16.6% uptime over 24 hours.

The free plan allows 50 monitors checked every 5 minutes, with email alerts and 1 status page. Keyword, heartbeat and API monitors, groups, 1-minute checks and several locations are paid. SSL certificate and domain checks are only in Solo, Team and Scale.

The cheapest paid plan has fewer monitors than the free plan. At checkout Solo 10 was 108 euros a year for 10 monitors, or 228 euros a year for 50 monitors. The summary said this is an auto-renewal payment. We stopped before the card details.
The pricing page lists 3 months of data and monthly email reports for the first 3 months only on Free. We read this and did not test it over time.
Deleting the account runs through Account details: UptimeRobot sends a verification email, after which all account information, monitors, logs and settings are lost and cannot be recovered.
not_tested: We did not watch the original sign-up; the account was already open when our session began.
Paid monitor types, SMS and voice alerts, a published status page, integrations, the API and MCP, and the mobile app were out of scope.
We did not contact support, invite anyone, enter card details, or export and re-import data.
The irreversible account deletion is left to the account owner.
We did not examine roles, API entitlement or a downgrade.
Session date 15 November 2026, Europe/Amsterdam time. Our clock readings are approximate and not a benchmark.
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
